subject: RTT surge — PulseRx hosted API: suspected cross-region routing misconfig
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@pulserx.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@pulserx.com
Date: 2027-09-12T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 RTT spike (hosted API) - urgent

Hi Hannah,

We started seeing a sharp degradation in RTT and an uptick in 5xx errors against the Redwood hosted API starting ~08:20 PDT. p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~1.2s; p99 is now in the 1.6–2.2s range. Also seeing a small but noticeable increase in 503s for streaming requests.

This is affecting our UI render times and a few background jobs. Our SREs captured traces for a few requests and we've attached a short sample. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (routing, peering, region preferences)? We need an ETA and mitigation steps — this is customer-impacting for us.

Sample: request ids xq3a, xq3b, xq3c; spike window 08:18–08:50.

Thanks,
Olivia
Principal SRE, PulseRx

Attachments: trace-20270912-0812.json (3 traces)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@pulserx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 RTT spike (hosted API) - urgent

Olivia — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm escalating to SRE now and copying Marissa (CS) and Jonas (SRE lead). We're treating this as a high-priority incident.

Immediate asks: can you confirm the client region for those request ids (us-west-2 vs us-east-1)? Also: are you seeing errors for all routes or a specific model/route?

Next steps from our side: Jonas will collect service-side traces and routing tables, and we will confirm whether a routing change or peering event occurred. I'll share an interim mitigation and an ETA within 30 minutes.

— Hannah
Director, Support Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p95/p99 RTT spike (hosted API) - urgent

Hannah / Marissa,

Preliminary findings from the control-plane and traffic taps: around 08:15 PDT an infra rollout adjusted the geo-routing policy used by the hosted API ingress. A new preference rule that was supposed to affect eu-west-only requests was incorrectly tagged and started applying to a subset of US customer prefixes (Pulserx included). As a result, traffic from some US client IP ranges began being routed via eu-west edges, introducing cross-region hops and the RTT regression you see.

What I ran:
- Compared routing policy set (route-diff.patch attached).
- Correlated request ids Olivia sent -> looked up ingress edge mapping and saw eu-west egress for paths that previously stayed in us-west.
- Extracted p95/p99 CSV (attached) showing a location-based split.

Mitigation plan (immediate):
1) Roll back the offending routing rule (rolling rev) — will be enacted at 09:40 PDT.
2) Apply a per-customer override (Pulserx) ensuring US prefixes prefer US edges — in-progress.
3) Throttle reroute to avoid cache-eviction storms.

I'll run the rollback and will confirm once RTTs start to return to baseline. ETA for rollback completion: ~10–12 minutes after start, then another 10–20m for metrics to reflect.

Attachments: route-diff.patch, p95-report.csv

-Jonas
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@pulserx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 RTT spike (hosted API) - interim mitigation

Olivia — quick update: our SRE lead (Jonas) identified an incorrect geo-routing tag deployed in an infra rollout that caused some US traffic to prefer eu-west edges. Jonas is rolling back the change now and applying a per-account routing override for PulseRx.

What to expect: rollback started at 09:40 PDT; we expect to see p95 recover toward baseline (≤300ms) within ~20–30 minutes after completion. We'll keep you posted on progress and will follow up with a detailed incident timeline and RCA.

As this affected PulseRx production latency, we're prepared to offer a service credit for the impacted window; Marissa will coordinate next steps if you want to pursue that.

Would you prefer a short call (15m) to walk through the mitigation and next steps?

Thanks for flagging this quickly — we'll remain on it until you confirm normal behavior.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Support Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@pulserx.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@pulserx.com
Date: 2027-09-12T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 RTT spike (hosted API) - interim mitigation

Hannah / team — thanks for the rapid response and the clear mitigation plan. We confirm client-side RTTs returned to normal around 10:20 PDT and our monitoring shows p95 back to ~230–260ms. We will take you up on the RCA and potential credit; please route the details to our procurement contact (procurement@pulserx.com) and cc me.

A quick ask for the RCA: can you include the git/release id that introduced the incorrect tag, and confirm whether auto-deploy safeguards will be tightened to prevent tag bleed in the future?

Thanks — Olivia
Principal SRE, PulseRx
